method: Per-station features joined by station name; median impute; drop constant or near-constant columns (one value in >= 95% of rows) and exact duplicates (|r| > 0.999); z-score; PCA (sklearn), UMAP (umap-learn, n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.3), t-SNE (perplexity 20); k-means groups on the first 8 PCs (80% variance), k chosen by silhouette.
pc1_top: +utilisation %, +utilisation 00-06, +utilisation at peak hour, +signals per km, +junctions per km
pc2_top: +multi-pump dispatch rate, +pumps, +multi-pump dispatches, −% of year all engines out, −% own-area calls covered by others
trip_and_model_metrics: 2025 trips from data/processed/lfb_travel_training.csv grouped by deployed_from_station; LightGBM error is held out (model trained 2021-24); cached in station_trip_metrics_2025.csv

not_joined.validation/closure_2014*: the 10 stations closed in 2014 are not current stations
not_joined.placement/tradeoff, tradeoff_busy, slow_: layout level with scenario x alpha keys that do not match the named layouts; left out of the layout PCA

honesty: Descriptive only. Many inputs measure the same thing (incidents, calls/day, engine hours, multi-dispatches all track demand), so PCA axes are dominated by whichever theme has the most columns; read loadings, not just positions. Area-map metrics give each map cell to its crow-fly nearest station, which is not the LFB station ground. Plan metrics come from specific planner runs with their own demand years. UMAP/t-SNE distances are only meaningful locally; their axes have no units. Groups are k-means on ~100 points with modest silhouette, so treat them as a reading aid, not station types.
